concepts.definition: Using two separate thresholds for switching on and switching off. Between the thresholds, the system keeps its previous state.
concepts.example: With the target at 22 °C, the heater switches on at 21.5 °C and off at 22.5 °C.
concepts.pitfall: Using a single threshold: when the temperature wobbles around the threshold, the relay switches on and off very fast.

concepts.definition: A design in which the system is in exactly one state at any moment. The thermostat's three states are KAPALI (off), ISITIYOR (heating) and AYAR (setting); each state has a set relay output and leaving condition.
concepts.example: The relay output is worked out from the state: digitalWrite(ROLE, durum == ISITIYOR ? HIGH : LOW);
concepts.pitfall: Writing the states as scattered ifs: the question of which state should keep the relay on gets out of control.

concepts.definition: The NTC and a fixed resistor make a voltage divider; from the ADC value, R = 10000 × ADC / (1023 − ADC) gives the NTC's resistance, and the β formula gives the temperature. As it warms up, the NTC's resistance falls.
concepts.example: With ADC = 512, R ≈ 10 kΩ, so about 25 °C.
concepts.pitfall: Swapping the places of the NTC and the fixed resistor: the reading works backwards.

concepts.term: Saving the setting with a delay
concepts.definition: Waiting until the user has finished adjusting (here, 2 seconds after the last press) and writing to the EEPROM once.
concepts.example: Five presses in a row are saved with a single EEPROM.update call.
concepts.pitfall: Writing to the EEPROM on every button press: needless writes use up its lifetime.

concepts.definition: At start-up, the value read from the EEPROM is checked to see whether it is in the valid range (10-35); if not, the default (22) is used. The buttons also keep the target in this range.
concepts.example: An empty EEPROM gives 255; because 255 is bigger than 35, the target becomes 22.
concepts.pitfall: Taking an empty EEPROM that reads as 255 for a valid target: the heater stays on all the time.

quiz.prompt: In the thermostat, ADC = 600 was read from pin A2. The fixed resistor is 10 kΩ and the formula R = 10000 × ADC / (1023 − ADC) is used. About how many ohms is the NTC's resistance? (Round to the nearest whole number.)
quiz.explanation: R = 10000 × 600 / (1023 − 600) = 6,000,000 / 423 ≈ 14,184 Ω. Because the resistance is bigger than 10 kΩ, the NTC is colder than 25 °C (an NTC's resistance falls as it warms up).

22.0 > 21.5: it stays KAPALI (0). 21.4 ≤ 21.5: ISITIYOR (1). 21.8 and 22.4 are below the switch-off threshold of 22.5: the relay stays on (1, 1). 22.6 ≥ 22.5: KAPALI (0). 22.2 is above the switch-on threshold of 21.5: it stays off (0). Result: 0 1 1 1 0 0.

The switch-off threshold in the ISITIYOR state should be hedef + HISTEREZIS. If minus is written, the switch-on and switch-off thresholds fall on the same number (target − 0.5); when the temperature drops below 21.5 the heater switches on, and as soon as the temperature rises a little it switches off straight away. The point of hysteresis is lost.

quiz.prompt: While the thermostat is running, the NTC's wire breaks, so the NTC drops out of the circuit (A2 is pulled to 5 V through the fixed resistor). How does the program work out the temperature, and what happens?
options: It thinks the temperature is very low and the heater stays on all the time
It thinks the temperature is very high and the heater switches off
It thinks the temperature is 0 °C and the program stops
quiz.explanation: When A2 is at 5 V, the ADC reaches its highest value (around 1022). The formula finds a very large resistance and the temperature comes out at about -77 °C: the program thinks it is 'very cold' and the relay stays on all the time. On a real heater this is dangerous; that is why a sensible-range check and a safety limit should be added.

quiz.prompt: The target 22 is already saved in the EEPROM. The user presses the up button 3 times and the down button 3 times, with 1 second between presses, then waits 2 seconds. The program uses EEPROM.update after the setting is finished. How many writes are made to the EEPROM in total?
quiz.explanation: Every press restarts the 2-second timer, so AYAR only finishes 2 seconds after the last press and a single update is called. Because the target goes 22 → 25 → 22, the value is the same as the one in the EEPROM; in this case update does not write at all. So 0 writes are made.
